subject: Insurance
title: The Great Fire of London
description: Learn The Great Fire of London in one minute.

hook.text: In 1666, a baker's oven burned 13,200 houses and 87 churches in four days. London had no fire insurance.

buildup.text: The fire destroyed 400 acres of the city. Rebuilding costs were astronomical.

discovery.text: Nicholas Barbon opened the first fire insurance office in 1681. For a yearly fee, he'd rebuild your house if it burned.

twist.text: Barbon also created the first fire brigade—but it only rescued insured buildings.

climax.text: The Great Fire created fire insurance, fire brigades, and building codes.

punchline.text: 13,200 homes, zero insurance. London's Great Fire invented fire coverage.

quiz.question: What did the Great Fire of London lead to?
